source_meta._title: using_item advancement trigger keeps being activated even after the item stops being used, after teleporting to another dimension

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 in a fresh vanilla single-player world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled as a practical safety choice: the report does not require a particular game mode, and Creative mode avoids environmental death after the datapack teleports the player to Overworld Y=-60. Install only the supplied MC-274372 datapack and any automatically enabled vanilla datapacks.
preconditions: A Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 installation is available; do not use fix version 24w33a for this reproduction.
The supplied attachment MC-274372.zip is available to the executor.
The executor can access the selected world's datapacks directory under <Minecraft game directory>/saves/<world name>/datapacks/.

The installed datapack must directly expose pack.mcmeta and the data directory at its root. If MC-274372.zip is only an outer wrapper around a datapack folder, install the inner datapack folder rather than leaving the extra wrapper level.
Use a fresh test world without another datapack defining the test namespace, advancement test:book, or function test:book.
The Use Item control must be available; its default input is the right mouse button.
Reserve at least three hotbar slots: one for the edible book, one for obsidian, and one for flint and steel.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft Launcher, select the exact Java Edition 1.21 installation, and start the game. Do not select the listed fix version 24w33a or a newer release.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.

steps.action: Create a fresh single-player world in Creative mode with commands or cheats enabled. No specific seed is required by the report. Enter a recognizable world name so its save directory can be found afterward.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new Creative-mode world and can open chat and execute commands.

steps.action: Press Esc, choose Save and Quit to Title, and wait for the world to finish closing before modifying its files.
steps.success_cue: The Singleplayer or main-title screen is visible and the test world is no longer open.

steps.action: Open the test world's datapacks directory in the filesystem: <Minecraft game directory>/saves/<world name>/datapacks/. Create the datapacks directory only if it is absent.
steps.success_cue: The filesystem view is open at the datapacks directory belonging to the same world created in step 2.

steps.action: Install the supplied MC-274372 datapack. First inspect MC-274372.zip: if pack.mcmeta and data are directly at the archive root, place that zip in the datapacks directory. If the archive instead contains one folder and that inner folder contains pack.mcmeta and data, extract or copy that inner folder into the datapacks directory. Do not leave pack.mcmeta hidden behind an unnecessary extra folder level.
steps.success_cue: One installed zip or folder in the world's datapacks directory directly contains pack.mcmeta and data, including the supplied test:book advancement and reward function.

steps.action: Return to Minecraft, open Singleplayer, select the same test world, and enter it. Wait until surrounding chunks render and normal movement is responsive.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the same Creative test world and the terrain is fully responsive.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, type the reload command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Datapack reloading completes without a red parsing, missing-function, or incompatible-pack error in chat.

steps.action: Press T, execute the datapack-list command, and inspect the enabled-pack list for the installed MC-274372 pack. Do not continue if the supplied pack is listed only as available or disabled.
steps.success_cue: The supplied MC-274372 file or folder appears in the enabled datapack list.

steps.action: Press T, enter the report's give command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Preserve the component syntax and numeric values exactly as supplied.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that a book was given, and a book item is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Locate the newly given book and move it into a reserved hotbar slot, such as the first slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory. Leave the book there while preparing the portal.
steps.success_cue: The edible book occupies a known hotbar slot and is not confused with another ordinary book.

steps.action: While using the Creative inventory, open the Search Items tab, obtain at least 14 obsidian blocks and one flint and steel, and put them in hotbar slots other than the book's slot. Close the inventory with E when finished.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains the edible book, at least 14 obsidian, and one flint and steel in distinct slots.

steps.action: Move to a clear area. Select the obsidian and build an upright rectangular Nether portal frame that is four blocks wide and five blocks tall on its outside edges, leaving a two-block-wide by three-block-high empty opening inside. Using 14 obsidian allows all four corners to be filled.
steps.success_cue: A complete upright obsidian frame surrounds an empty 2-by-3-block interior opening.

steps.action: Select the flint and steel, aim at an exposed face of an obsidian block bordering the bottom of the frame's interior, and use the item with right-click.
steps.success_cue: The portal's interior fills with the animated purple Nether-portal surface.

steps.action: Walk into the purple portal surface and remain inside it without stepping out until the dimension transition starts.
steps.success_cue: The dimension-loading screen or portal transition begins.

steps.action: Wait for the Nether destination to finish loading. Do not begin the item-use test while terrain is still loading or player movement is unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: Nether terrain and its reddish ambience are visible, surrounding chunks have rendered, and player movement responds normally.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the edible book by pressing that slot's number key or scrolling to it. Do not merely keep the book elsewhere in the inventory.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing the book
steps.success_cue: The book's hotbar slot is highlighted and the book is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Press F3, or the system's equivalent Debug Screen input, so the debug overlay can be used to recognize the cross-dimension teleport and destination coordinates. Keep the book selected.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay is visible and displays the player's current XYZ coordinates while the book remains selected.

steps.action: Press and continuously hold Use Item while the edible book is selected. The default input is the right mouse button. Do not release the input in the Nether and do not switch hotbar slots.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold Use Item (default: right mouse button)
steps.success_cue: The book-use action has started, or the dimension transition begins immediately in response to starting it; the Use Item input remains held.

steps.action: Continue holding Use Item until the datapack transfers the player from the Nether to the Overworld. Watch the debug coordinates and dimension transition; the supplied reward function targets X=0, Y=-60, Z=0 with yaw 0 and pitch 0. Keep the same book slot selected throughout the transfer.
steps.success_cue: The Nether is no longer the active dimension, and the player has arrived in the Overworld at or effectively at XYZ 0, -60, 0 with the book still selected.

steps.action: As soon as the Overworld destination is reached, release the Use Item input completely. Do not use the book again, do not switch hotbar slots, and do not close the world before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.exact_input: Release Use Item (default: release the right mouse button)
steps.success_cue: The right mouse button or rebound Use Item control is no longer pressed; the edible book remains selected in the active hotbar slot; and the player remains at the Overworld destination immediately after the release.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just arrived in the Overworld at approximately XYZ 0, -60, 0 after beginning to use the edible book in the Nether. Use Item has now been released completely, the same edible book remains selected, and no further item use or hotbar-slot change has been performed. Begin observation immediately from this state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, world seed, single-player versus dedicated server, or a required portal location. This plan uses a fresh Creative single-player world as the simplest safe execution path and does not treat Creative mode as a bug requirement.

The report comments state that an earlier attachment was an outer zip containing a datapack folder and that a moderator corrected it. The raw report does not expose the current archive's internal file tree, so installation is conditional on whether pack.mcmeta and data are at the archive root.

The report supplies the advancement and function excerpts but not the full pack.mcmeta or directory tree. This plan therefore relies on the supplied corrected attachment instead of attempting to reconstruct the datapack manually.

The report does not specify whether controls were rebound. Right mouse button, E, T, W, and F3 refer to the standard default controls; use the corresponding bound actions if the test installation differs.

The report does not explicitly instruct the player to release Use Item immediately after arriving in the Overworld, but release is necessary to establish the reported condition in which the item is no longer being used. The release has therefore been made the final trigger action.

source_meta._title: The `fall_after_explosion` advancement trigger does not work with TNT anymore

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1.2 in a fresh, disposable singleplayer world. Use Creative mode with commands enabled so the attached datapack can be checked and the TNT launcher can be assembled without unrelated resource gathering. Use the exact attached datapack archive named "tnt test 1.21.11-26.1.zip" and the attached video "We_Have_Liftoff_26_1_x.mp4" as the blueprint for the launcher. Do not use 26.2 Snapshot 7 or a later fixed version.
preconditions: The official Minecraft Launcher has an installation for Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1.2.
The three report attachments are locally available, especially "tnt test 1.21.11-26.1.zip" and "We_Have_Liftoff_26_1_x.mp4".
Use a new world so the advancement from the attached datapack has not already been granted.
Use the datapack method listed as method 1 in the report; do not also install BlazeandCave's Advancement Pack or modify a vanilla advancement, because either would introduce unnecessary variables.
No gameplay mods, server plugins, or additional datapacks are enabled.

The launcher must use TNT entities as shown in the attached video. Do not substitute wind charges, TNT minecarts, beds, respawn anchors, or another explosion source because the advancement condition specifically tests a cause entity of type "minecraft:tnt".
Build in an open area with enough unobstructed vertical space for the player to rise at least 100 blocks above the launch position.
Keep a copy of the disposable world or be prepared to create another fresh world if the one-use TNT launcher is accidentally activated before the player is correctly positioned.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1.2, and start the game. Do not select the listed fix version, 26.2 Snapshot 7.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the title screen and identifies the running version as 26.1.2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World to open the new-world configuration screen.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Give the world a recognizable name, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure commands or cheats are enabled. Creative mode is an execution convenience and does not replace the TNT launch condition.
steps.success_cue: The new-world screen shows Creative mode and commands enabled.

steps.action: From the new-world screen, navigate to the Data Packs configuration. In the standard Java Edition world-creation interface, open the More tab or page, select Data Packs, and then select Open Pack Folder.
steps.exact_input: More -> Data Packs -> Open Pack Folder
steps.success_cue: The operating system opens the datapacks folder associated with the world being created.

steps.action: Copy the exact attached archive into the opened datapacks folder. Keep it as a ZIP archive unless Minecraft fails to detect it; do not edit its advancement JSON or pack metadata.
steps.success_cue: The file "tnt test 1.21.11-26.1.zip" is present in the opened datapacks folder.

steps.action: Return to Minecraft. If the pack appears under Available, select its pack icon or arrow to move it to Selected. Confirm the datapack selection and return to the world-creation screen. If the game reports a fatal validation error and will not enable the pack, stop rather than rewriting the attachment.
steps.success_cue: The attached datapack is listed as selected or enabled, with no fatal validation error preventing world creation.

steps.action: Select Create New World. Wait until the player appears in the world, nearby chunks have rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a responsive 26.1.2 world and surrounding terrain has loaded.

steps.action: Verify that the attached datapack is enabled. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the enabled datapacks and includes the custom pack loaded from the attached archive; no datapack loading error is displayed.

steps.action: Outside Minecraft, open the attached video "We_Have_Liftoff_26_1_x.mp4". Review or pause it at frames that clearly show the complete launcher, including its dimensions, block spacing, water placement, TNT positions, redstone or timing components, player launch position, and activation method. Keep the video available while building.
steps.success_cue: The executor has a visible reference for the complete 26.1-series launcher and its activation sequence.

steps.action: In Minecraft, move to a flat, open build site. Look upward and confirm there is no roof, overhang, tree canopy, or other obstruction in the vertical launch path. If necessary, clear the site using Creative mode.
steps.success_cue: A flat construction area and an unobstructed vertical launch path of more than 100 blocks are available.

steps.action: Obtain the blocks and components shown in the attached video from the Creative inventory. Press E to open the inventory, use the Search Items field to locate each required item, and place each item in the hotbar, which is the row of nine slots at the bottom of the inventory. Do not acquire a wind charge or substitute a different explosive for TNT.
steps.success_cue: Every block and component visible in the video's launcher, including TNT, is available in the Creative inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Recreate the non-explosive structure of the launcher block-for-block from the attached 26.1 video. Preserve the video's dimensions, spacing, elevations, containment blocks, slabs or partial blocks, water sources, and the orientation of directional blocks. Use right-click to place blocks and left-click to remove any incorrectly placed block.
steps.success_cue: The launcher's structural frame and any water containment match the attached video's arrangement, with no TNT placed prematurely unless the video requires it during construction.

steps.action: Place the launcher's redstone and timing components exactly as shown in the video. Preserve component orientation, repeater delay settings, wiring connections, and the state of any lever, button, pressure plate, or other activation control. Keep the launcher unpowered while assembling it.
steps.success_cue: The completed control circuit visually matches the video and has not yet initiated a TNT fuse.

steps.action: Place the exact number of ordinary TNT blocks in the exact positions shown in the video. Do not replace them with TNT minecarts and do not manually ignite any TNT before all positions have been checked.
steps.success_cue: All TNT positions match the attached video, the TNT remains unprimed, and the launcher is ready for a single activation.

steps.action: Compare the finished launcher against the clearest full-contraption frame in "We_Have_Liftoff_26_1_x.mp4". Check the structure from the same viewing direction and correct any differences in block count, block orientation, water placement, TNT placement, wiring, or player position markers before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The completed launcher matches the report video closely enough that its TNT timing and launch direction are preserved.

steps.action: Move the player into the precise launch position shown in the video. Make sure the player is standing rather than using Creative flight: if currently flying, press the jump control twice, default Space twice, and settle onto the launch surface. Do not hold movement, jump, sneak, or sprint.
steps.exact_input: Space twice only if Creative flight is active
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary, affected by gravity, and aligned with the TNT launcher at the same launch position shown in the video.

steps.action: Press F3 to display the debug overlay and record the player's current Y coordinate as Y_start. Leave the overlay visible if it does not obstruct activation; otherwise record the value and close it with F3. The launch must reach at least Y_start + 100.
steps.success_cue: The launch-position Y coordinate has been recorded and a target value equal to Y_start plus 100 has been calculated.

steps.action: Activate the launcher exactly once using the same control and input shown in the attached video. For example, if the demonstrated control is a button or lever, aim the crosshair at it and right-click once; do not repeatedly toggle it. Immediately release all movement controls.
steps.success_cue: The launcher's TNT fuse or demonstrated redstone activation sequence has started while the player remains in the launch position.

steps.action: Remain in place until the TNT detonates and launches the player upward. Do not press Space twice, enable Creative flight, move out of the launch column, or use commands during the ascent.
steps.success_cue: The player has been propelled upward by ordinary TNT and is ascending without player-controlled flight.

steps.action: During the ascent, monitor the debug Y coordinate if available. Allow the player to continue upward until the coordinate has increased by at least 100 blocks from Y_start. Do not wait for the player to land and do not activate the launcher a second time.
steps.success_cue: The player has reached an altitude of at least Y_start + 100 as a result of the TNT launch.

steps.action: Release every movement input and allow gravity to take over at the apex. The precise advancement-triggering moment is when the TNT-launched player stops rising and begins falling. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately at that transition, before landing or performing another action.
steps.success_cue: The player has just transitioned from upward motion to downward motion after rising at least 100 blocks from the TNT explosion launch.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just begun descending after being launched at least 100 blocks upward by the video-matched ordinary-TNT launcher in the fresh 26.1.2 world, with the attached datapack enabled. Begin advancement observation immediately; do not wait for landing, reactivate the launcher, open menus, or use commands first.
uncertainties: The raw report does not textually describe the TNT launcher's block list, dimensions, TNT count, redstone timings, water layout, launch position, or activation control. Those details exist only in the attached videos, so the plan must use "We_Have_Liftoff_26_1_x.mp4" as the authoritative visual blueprint rather than fabricate a different launcher.

The exact namespace and advancement identifier inside "tnt test 1.21.11-26.1.zip" are not supplied. A fresh world is therefore used to ensure the criterion starts ungranted without inventing an /advancement revoke command target.

The structured Affects versions field lists 26.1.2, while the description says "26.1+" and the original Steps to Reproduce say 26.1. Per affected-version selection policy, this plan uses the exact structured affected version 26.1.2.

The attachment filename and description explicitly mention compatibility with 26.1 rather than specifically 26.1.2. The plan assumes the attached pack remains loadable in the listed affected patch 26.1.2. If Minecraft rejects it with a fatal datapack-format error, execution is blocked and the attachment should not be silently rewritten.

The report includes a comparison run in Minecraft 1.21.11. This plan stops at the trigger in the first formally listed affected version, 26.1.2, as required for bug reproduction. A separate 1.21.11 control world can be prepared using the same archive and its corresponding video if the observation system also requires regression comparison.
